answer: A beacon registry can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a stake and post a verifiable work proof before its identity is listed. New identities start at the glacier-slow trust tier: they may observe but cannot transact until peers attest their behavior over time. Reaching the summit tier requires sustained honest work plus stake that is slashed on fraud. An attacker must therefore fund many stakes and burn weeks of compute per fake identity, while a single honest agent pays once.
